name: Smurfit Westrock

logo.source: company site header SVG (smurfitwestrock.com, SW_Logo_169x40.svg); Wikipedia infobox PNG is only 238 px wide

description: Smurfit Westrock makes corrugated cardboard boxes and the containerboard paper they are made from, plus folding cartons and other consumer packaging. It was created in July 2024 by merging Ireland's Smurfit Kappa with US-based WestRock, so 2025 is the first full year (net sales $31.2B versus $21.1B in 2024 when WestRock counted only from July). It owns 57 paper mills and 450 converting plants in 40 countries and sells boxes to food, consumer goods, e-commerce and industrial customers, mostly at prices that move with the cost of paper and recycled fiber. Profit swings with containerboard prices and mill utilisation, which is why it announced mill closures in 2025 and booked $385M of impairment and restructuring costs.

businessLines.description: Containerboard, corrugated packaging, consumer packaging (folding cartons, paperboard) and related businesses in the US, Canada and Mexico.

businessLines.description: Containerboard, corrugated packaging, bag-in-box and consumer packaging across Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific; legacy Smurfit Kappa heartland.

businessLines.name: LATAM
businessLines.how: Sells boxes and containerboard to regional food, agriculture and consumer customers; much of the wood fiber comes from owned plantations.
businessLines.description: Corrugated packaging, containerboard and forestry in Latin America (Brazil, Mexico, Colombia and others); owns forests and plantations.
